title: Crushed concrete specimen between compression platens with debris
objects_and_counts: One crushed/consolidated concrete specimen is visible in the centre of the image, vertically compressed between two square metal platen faces.
Two metal platen faces are visible: one at the top of the specimen and one at the bottom; both platen faces are roughly square and show metallic/brown discoloration.
Two vertical cylindrical/round columns with a dark blue colour are visible at the left and right edges of the image; both are partially visible and appear to be part of the test frame.
Many broken fragments and flakes of concrete debris lie around the base platen and on the lower surface; an exact count cannot be determined from the image.
One red insulated wire is visible running across the foreground over the debris toward the bottom centre of the image.
One circular lower platen or base plate is visible under the debris at the bottom of the image (partially obscured by rubble).
spatial_relations: The crushed concrete specimen is located centrally and is directly between the upper square platen face and the lower square platen face, indicating a vertical compression orientation.
Broken concrete fragments are scattered around and on top of the lower platen and lie in the foreground in front of the specimen.
The red wire lies across the lower platen area and across the debris toward the front edge of the image.

The two dark blue vertical columns are positioned left and right near the specimen and appear to form the vertical supports of the test frame; the upper platen is attached above the specimen and the lower platen sits on a circular base under the debris.
colours_and_materials: The specimen and fragments are predominantly grey concrete with visible lighter-coloured aggregate pieces (white and light grey) and occasional small orange-brown particles.
The upper and lower platen faces have a brownish/metallic discoloration (possible rust or patina) and appear metallic.
The vertical support columns are a dark blue colour.
A conspicuous red insulated wire is visible across the lower area.
The lower circular base/plate under the debris appears dark grey to black.
